rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance (Just Cause Eviction)
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a legally defined 'just cause' (at-fault or no-fault) to terminate a residential tenancy, must give specified notices, and must provide relocation assistance for no-fault terminations.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental units in the City of San Diego subject to the ordinance; specific exemptions not detailed in this passage.
rules.penalty: Landlord liable to tenant in civil action for wrongful eviction for damages of at least 3x the actual economic damages; for failure to provide relocation assistance, liable for at least 3x the required relocation assistance plus actual economic damages; reasonable attorney's fees and costs may be awarded; remedies are cumulative.
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code § 98.0704 et seq.
rules.quoted_span: The purpose of the Ordinance is to require Just Cause for termination of residential tenancies consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2, to limit the reasons for termination of a residential tenancy, to require greater tenant relocation assistance in specified circumstances and to provide additional tenant protections.
